View. The building is the Town hall in the view r3. a two-storey red-brick town hall with cream limestone quoins, string courses and window surrounds, under a dark slate gable roof whose ridge runs along the long front, with a brick chimney stack with red pots at each end and a bell cupola with a slate dome and a gold finial in the middle of the ridge. The FRONT (the long wall) has a central cream-stone gable with a round clock face, a cream portico with columns over a forest-green double door, arched windows on two storeys in a regular rhythm, two hanging lanterns and two conifer planters beside the portico. One END is a brick gable with cream quoins and a stepped or scrolled cream gable edge, two columns of arched windows on two storeys and a small arched attic window. The back wall has the same quoins, string courses and windows and a plain green door instead of the portico; the other end is a brick gable like the first. r3: the building is turned 3 quarter turns clockwise seen from above, about the middle of its footprint, not mirrored; every part keeps its place on the building and moves with it, so: the long front with the clock gable, the portico and double door, the lanterns and planters and the arched windows stands at the lower-right side; the brick gable end with cream quoins, two columns of arched windows and the small arched attic window stands at the upper-right side; the long back wall (brick, quoins and string courses, windows, a plain green door; no clock gable, no portico, no planters, no lanterns) stands at the upper-left side; the other brick gable end (as the render has it) stands at the lower-left side.
